children: Cocoa futures on the ICE exchange hit three-week highs on Tuesday amid El Niño-linked hot, dry conditions in top grower Ivory Coast, while robusta coffee plumbed a fresh three-year low.
COCOA
* London cocoa
settled up £49, or 1.2%, at £4,191  per metric ton, having earlier hit its highest since early November at £4,223.
* Cocoa arrivals at ports in Ivory Coast were down 47.1% at 54,000 metric tons in the week ending November 22 versus the same period a year ago, exporters estimated.
* Cumulative arrivals for the 2026/27 marketing year have meanwhile reached just 367,500, down from 618,000 this time last year.
* The five-year average for this point in the season is 625,400 tons, broker ADMIS noted.
* On the weather front, little relief is expected over the week ahead, said the broker, with temperatures in Ivory Coast set to head higher and rains remaining light.
* New York cocoa
rose 2.2% to $5,413 a ton, having earlier hit its highest since early November at $5,481.
COFFEE
* Robusta coffee
settled down $41, or 1.4%, at $2,813 a ton, after setting a fresh three-year low of $2,801 as what is set to be a bumper harvest gets underway in top grower Vietnam.

* "The outlook remains very positive for Vietnam," said StoneX coffee analyst Leonardo Rossetti, adding that the country's coffee and cocoa association Vicofa estimated the crop at over 36 million bags, up 5% from last season.
* No. 3 grower Indonesia, meanwhile, continues to benefit from recent rains.
* Arabica coffee
fell 1.9% to $2.626 per lb, its lowest level in five months.
* ICE arabica stocks were last at their highest since late July at 272,868 bags >.

* "Strong Brazilian shipments and favourable arabica rainfall remain pressures, (though) nearby premiums continue to reflect limited immediate availability," said broker and consultant Michael J Nugent.
SUGAR
* Raw sugar
rose 0.3% to 17.66 cents per lb, after setting a three-month low of 16.82 cents on Friday.
* Ethanol prices in top grower Brazil are currently higher than the equivalent for sugar, which might lead cane mills to produce less of the sweetener and more of the biofuel.
* White sugar
fell 0.3% to $501 a ton.
